units.spine: Goods here change hands one at a time, and nothing in the place is arranged for more than that.
Every job here is somebody's second job.
Stock and people are kept close in, and the ground further out counts as abandoned.
The trouble here is the slow kind rather than the sudden kind, and the place has the room to work at it.
Warmholz bends this far and not much further.
The worsening is steady rather than sudden, and each season costs a little more than the one before.
The year closes near enough to level that the closing is watched.
Only a part of what happens here is ever spoken of, and nothing decides which part.
The place works on the terms it has, and what falls short is the terms and not the working.
A place this size ought to have more between its houses and whatever comes than this one has.
What protects Warmholz is that nobody has wanted it, and everybody here understands the arrangement.
Beyond the fields the place has no answer to what lives there, and nobody whose work it would be.
More goes on here than anybody looks into, though little of it is hidden.
Nothing in the hamlet is spare, and that is what a careful eye takes in first.
No practitioner lives here, no arrangement stands to bring one, and nobody expects either.
Food is not thought about here, and that is the most that can be said for anybody's food.
The houses stand a reasonable distance from the last place, and that is the whole of the reason for them.
A handful of roofs is the whole of Warmholz, and what keeps them here is the ground under them.
The people here are bound to one another the way any settled place is bound, and no further than that.
One loose end runs through the place, and one standing arrangement would tie it off.
